memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But now, please forgive their sin - but if not, then blot me out of the book you have written.'" - Exod 32:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most staggering prayers in all of Scripture. Moses offers himself. Blot me out instead of them.

Understand what he is asking. He is willing to lose his own place before God so that this stubborn, idolatrous people might be spared. Paul would later echo the same heart, wishing himself cut off for the sake of his own people (Rom 9:3).

Where does that kind of love come from? Not from human sentiment. It is a reflection of God's own heart, placed in a man.

And it points forward. Moses offered — but he could not accomplish it. He was a sinner himself; his own name could not purchase anyone's forgiveness. Only one Man could genuinely take another's place, and He did. Christ was cut off for us, made a curse for us, so that we might never be blotted out (Gal 3:13; 2 Cor 5:21).

Every believer's name is written in the Lamb's book of life (Rev 21:27) — not because our record is clean, but because His is.

If you have ever wondered how much you are loved, here is your answer. Moses was willing. Jesus actually did it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose salvation do you long for enough to sacrifice for?
2. Have you grasped that Christ was cut off so you would not be?
3. What does it mean to you that your name is written in His book?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You took my place. Thank You that I will never be blotted out because You were cut off for me. Amen.
